Finding space to pioneer
The intellectually edgy, kind and unstuffy independent school for girls in the heart of the City
This is City!
Watch to learn more about our distinctive and exciting school.
A message from the Head
This is a place of bold academic exploration and intellectual curiosity, which empowers girls to think independently and confidently.
Ready to pioneer
Our strategic development plan will ready our pupils in five key areas:
Ready to pioneer
Our strategic development plan will ready our pupils in five key areas:
Pupils are encouraged to try new ways of thinking and learning, exercising entrepreneurial and collaborative skills
Pupils engage fully in our renewed, individualised, sector-leading careers programme - City Futures - ensuring applicable skills are honed across the curriculum
Every pupil, whatever their contexts, feels heard and understood at school
Pupils understand themselves as global citizens, capitalising on the connections that our place in the City of London allows
Pupils seek to live and learn sustainably and adopt actions that have a positive impact on our place and planet
Admissions
We’re thrilled that you are thinking of joining our distinctive and grounded school. We aim to make the admissions process as stress-free as possible.

Open days
Our annual open mornings and afternoons offer an opportunity for parents and girls to meet the head, key staff, and current pupils, and to get a flavour of daily life at City.
Take a look inside
Click on the hotspots to explore some of the hidden areas of our building.

Learning
Pupils thrive in an environment in which learning is highly valued.
Wellbeing

Support us
City provides tangible proof that needs-blind access creates a thriving community where students can achieve, irrespective of their background. However, every year we are still forced to turn away pupils who deserve a City education, simply because we do not have the funds to support them.

pageCache.text:
Our ethos and strategic plan
Our ethos
Being a pupil at CLSG means being part of the City of London and part of the great tradition of people arriving in the City, learning, and working together to forge better lives for themselves and for the world.
We reflect the City’s pioneering energy in the liberal, scholarly education it offers and in our inclusivity. We encourage pupils’ curiosity and courage, emphasise respect, collaboration and connectedness for communal and individual success. We seek to build readiness for the world that our location and ethos so distinctly delivers.
Our values of respect, responsibility and resourcefulness underpin our ethos.
Our vision
We inspire our pupils to find their space to pioneer.
Our strategic development plan
We will ready our pupils in five key areas:
Our main school aims
Our strategic aims cover six key areas:
Pupils are academically curious and resourceful; they take risks, are ambitious and love learning for its own sake​.
Co-curricular & partnerships
Pupils contribute enthusiastically to co-curricular activities and partnerships and serve the communities around them with respect.
Pupils understand themselves, are listened to and take reflective ownership of their lives and are considerate of others.
High-calibre staff and inspirational teachers are empowered through outstanding professional development opportunities​​.
The management of the financial and human resources, and estates, is forward-looking, sustainable and compliant.
The school will be distinctive and understood, allowing it to attract a diverse intake of pupils and staff, and to influence wider debate.
Prize Day
Instagram
What happens when students are given the freedom to explore a topic that genuinely fascinates them? For our year 13 EPQ students, the answer is a year of fulfilling independent research, intellectual challenge and fascinating discoveries. Last week students presented their final projects, exploring topics ranging from ancient burial rituals and robotic surgery to reparations for the Marshall Islands and the experiences of female domestic workers in Hong Kong. Meet four of our students and discover where their curiosity took them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's welcome - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
Head’s welcome
Welcome to City of London School for Girls. Come on into our website and enjoy discovering what makes this such an exhilarating place to learn and work.
Being in the heart of the capital and right alongside all the cultural heritage of the Barbican and the professional powerhouses of the City defines the school and is part of what makes it so exciting, but the real excitement is found within the classrooms.
This is a place of brave academic enquiry, of intellectual wonder and of fiercely independent thinkers. It’s hard to convey the excitement of the learning in this school, but whether it’s recent year 7 projects on freedom, a year 12 bounding excitedly into my office with news of her publication in a national medical periodical or hearing about the sixth form genetic engineering project or the pupil talking about her published fanfiction, I am daily struck by its scholarly energy. This is a place where ideas in these rooms become almost become bigger than the people in them, where the structures of learning can become an escape from the self and identity. City is a school which never places any artificial division on our formal academic and co-curricular provision, but celebrates the wild adventure and the fun of learning wherever it is found.
It does so though without posture, or pose. We are a kind and compassionate place too, and our values of respect, responsibility and resourcefulness course through the concrete of our famous Barbican site. We are proud of our outstanding and individualised pastoral care, which encourages pupils to understand themselves and take considered and reflective ownership of their lives. We nurture an inclusive and kind community, which embraces the cultural and social mix in the school and world around us.
Pupils care about each other and the things that matter in life. They take themselves and their ambitions seriously and have a great deal of fun. We are so proud of all that our pupils achieve and contribute, finding opportunities to experiment and grow in confidence and serve the communities around them.
Our pupils are unfailingly good company; they regularly make me laugh and surprise me. Nothing can replace meeting them – or visiting our school, which really is a place of wonders. I do hope I can welcome you here very soon.
Jenny Brown, Headmistress

pageCache.pageTitle: About us - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
About us
'Pupils are inspired to find their space to pioneer by being given the freedom in almost all lessons to explore, discover and create tasks for themselves, while being encouraged to do so by supportive, but highly challenging teaching.'
- Independent Schools Inspectorate
City of London School for Girls is an independent day school for pupils aged 11-18 situated in the heart of the Barbican. Opened in 1894, the school provides an outstanding education for able students from all backgrounds, cultures and faiths. We capitalise on our location to attract students from all over Greater London and beyond, and give them access to every learning opportunity our capital has to offer.
Academic yet unstuffy, modern yet acutely aware of its history, diverse yet with a strong sense of identity, our school defies easy categorisation. This is best demonstrated by our unique geography, nestled between the brutalist Barbican and looming Roman walls. Ours is an intellectually edgy, unassuming and unpretentious environment, unshackled by tradition, and imbued with a relaxed excellence. This is a refreshing and modern place in which to learn.
Welcome to City of London School for Girls. Come on into our website and enjoy discovering what makes this such an exhilarating place to learn and work.
Head’s welcome
Our ethos and strategic plan
Inspirational learning, exciting partnerships and a strong culture of self-reflection in the heart of the capital will grow a new generation of pioneering young people.
Learning
Pupils thrive in an environment in which learning is highly valued.

Governors
City of London School for Girls is a proud member of the City of London Corporation. The Corporation supports the school by appointing a board of governors, whose individual tenures last for between one and three years. The governors’ board brings together a vast amount of professional experience and enthusiasm for our community, which they use to guide and counsel the school.
Governors

pageCache.pageTitle: History - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
History
On his death in 1881, William Ward left a generous bequest in his will with the intention of transforming the lives of young women through an inspiring and empowering education. A successful merchant from Brixton (then a leafy country neighbourhood on the outskirts of London) Ward left a significant portion of his wealth to the foundation and maintenance of a high school for girls to be called by the name and known forever as "The City of London School for Girls founded by William Ward". The school opened its doors on Carmelite Street in 1894. 130 years later, a lot has changed.

pageCache.pageTitle: School structure - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
School structure
The school is divided into three main sections: the lower school (years 7 and 8), the senior school (years 9, 10 and 11) and the sixth form (years 12 and 13). Read more from the heads of sections below.
Lower school
The lower school is made up of years 7 and 8. Joining year 7 can feel a daunting experience, so our main aim is to make the transition as welcoming and easy as possible, and to make the start really exciting and fun. We strive to imbue the pupils with a real delight in learning for its own sake and to ensure they have strong friendships.
Senior school
In year 9, pupils move into the senior school. These next three years are an incredibly exciting time, with pupils gaining a greater sense of independence and self. It is also another period of transition as they embark first on their GCSE courses and then decide on their A Level choices.
Sixth form
Many students comment on the fact the sixth form feels like a very different experience from the lower and senior schools. Smaller classes, free periods, use of the sixth form centre, own clothes and greater independence and responsibility all contribute towards this feeling.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
Partnerships
'Pupils have a strong sense of social justice and spoke of being empowered by the school to make a difference... Pupils readily embrace the many opportunities that arise from the school's extensive partnership work.'
- Independent Schools Inspectorate
Partnerships
City of London School for Girls is acutely aware of its responsibility to engage with the world outside the school, both as part of the community in London and more broadly in promoting international links. We are thoroughly committed to fostering a concern for, and engagement with, the wider world both through our charity work and through our partnership programme. We want our students to develop a strong sense of social responsibility and an understanding of their role in addressing the needs of others. Please see our partnerships impact report below or read our partnership strategy here.
Family of schools
The City of London Corporation has one maintained primary school, eleven sponsored academies as part of the City of London Academies Trust, and supports four independent schools. They are collectively known as ‘the City of London Family of Schools’ and multiple ventures are organised across this structure.
The Big Sing
As part of the London Handel Festival, over 380 pupils from eight partner schools came together for The Big Sing in collaboration with the London Handel Orchestra. Through regular workshops in singing, literacy, and history, pupils celebrated London’s musical heritage and the joy of community performance.
City SPARC
City SPARC is a pioneering science partnership between CLS and CLSG, connecting year 12 pupils from six schools with PhD mentors to conduct original research. The year-long programme builds practical STEM skills, from experimental design to data analysis, with many participants achieving prestigious CREST Gold accreditation.
LSE Mentorpreneurship
We enjoy an active partnership with the London School of Economics, which each year leads the LSE Mentorpreneurship Programme. This three-and-a-half day scheme is based on the LSE campus, and invites year 9 pupils from CLSG and other partner schools to come together in mixed school teams to design a product which solves a current real-world problem. Attending pupils also have the opportunity to network, learn from, and be mentored by professionals, and leave the programme with a better understanding of how a business and workplace operate.
HerAI Conference
In November 2025 we hosted our first HerAI conference. Year 12 students from CLSG and other partner schools were invited to hear from four trailblazing voices shaping the forefront of artificial intelligence; Joanna Shan from Google DeepMind, Amy Gaeta from the University of Cambridge, Charlotte Wood from Schroders and Laura Bates, best-selling author and founder of the Everyday Sexism Project. Each guest offered a fresh gendered perspective of this ever-evolving field, discussing the ethics, risks, but also incredible potential of AI.
Family of Schools Debating Competitions
Debating is a big part of life at CLSG, and we are delighted that since autumn 2025 we have begun to deliver termly Family of Schools debating competitions. Competitions have either a primary or secondary focus, with pupils coming together in their school teams to develop their knowledge and understanding of formal debating. A particular highlight of each competition is some of our experienced year 11/12 debaters supporting the events by judging the competitions.
Climate Action Conferences with Schroders
We are delighted that each year our partner in industry Schroders, an asset management company, hosts a Sustainability Conference aimed at eco-minded year 12 students from across the Family of Schools. Each conference provides students the opportunity to listen to and connect with industry professionals working within the square mile. The most recent conference, held in March 2026, focused on ‘Climate Innovation in the Food Supply Chain’.
Maths network
Now in its fourth academic year, this maths network enables collaboration between colleagues across the Family of Schools. It enables a focus on pedagogy, curriculum and assessment strategies. It also sparks cross-phase as well as primary and secondary-specific dialogues to take place, facilitating a rich exchange of ideas across a group of schools.
Leadership Networking lunch
Each autumn term, CLSG welcomes year 12 and year 13 pupil leaders from CLS, CLSG, Islington Collegiate Sixth Form, and City of London Academy Shoreditch Park for a Leadership Networking lunch. Attending pupils spend the afternoon networking and sharing their experience of the benefits and challenges of pupil leadership.
Oracy network
We are delighted to be at the forefront of cross-phase, co-chaired professional network groups across the Family of Schools in key areas of oracy and maths. Groups of key practitioners from across the Family of Schools meet on a termly basis to share best practice and jointly address shared problems for the benefit of pupils across the group.
Aldgate Sports Masterclass
We are thrilled that we now run a yearly sports masterclass with year 5 pupils from The Aldgate School. Each January pupils come to CLSG for a morning carousel of high-energy sessions exploring a range of sports, led by our Sports-Captains. Last year pupils had sessions on fencing, netball, football, and gymnastics.
Higher education support
Our careers department continues to share career development advice and resources across the academy and independent school network supported by the Corporation of London. Our higher education evening and other careers events are open to attendees from across the family of schools and CLSG staff provides bespoke interview support and guidance for pupils aspiring to apply to Oxbridge. They also offer a US universities talk to support students with overseas applications.
Linklaters
Since autumn 2020, CLSG has forged a valued partnership with leading law firm, Linklaters, to provide learning and development opportunities to pupils from across the Family of Schools. We are delighted that each year Linklaters generously hosts both a public speaking workshop for year 6 and year 7 pupils as well as a ‘careers in law’ insight day for year 12s.
Primary summer school
Each summer, we welcome pupils from our partner primary schools for three days of hands-on learning, offering a taste of secondary school life. Pupils take part in a variety of activities in the heart of the City. In summer 2025, pupils experienced a ‘skulls workshop’, handled Roman artefacts at the Guildhall, and met renowned children’s author Josh Lacey.
Reading mentors
Now in its sixth year, the reading mentors programme at City is an established volunteering opportunity for CLSG pupils across the school. In partnership with Galleywall Primary School, pupils from both schools meet weekly for one-to-one sessions, developing confidence on reading skills, comprehension and vocabulary building.
IntoUniversity
At the beginning of each academic year, year 12 students from CLSG and CLS have the opportunity to become a volunteer for our partner charity IntoUniversity. Becoming an academic support volunteer requires students to spend an evening each week tutoring/mentoring pupils at the IntoUniversity centre of their choice. Before becoming a volunteer, students from CLS and CLSG come together for a day of training to prepare them to best support the sessions they will deliver. This partnership provides our students with an incredible leadership opportunity whilst also supporting many students across the centres achieve more academically.
City of London School
We have a strong relationship with our brother school, situated just up the road beside St Paul’s Cathedral. Our students collaborate on joint plays, musical projects, and charity initiatives, as well as forming strong social connections outside school hours.
iGEM
The iGEM Foundation is an independent, non-profit organisation dedicated to the advancement of synthetic biology, education and competition. For the past few years, CLSG has been entering the iGEM competition as a team in partnership with participants from City of London School. This year, a joint team of pupils from CLSG and CLS have worked together on a project to address the issue posed by nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions in the NHS sector. iGEM is a brilliant opportunity for students to engineer creative solutions for problems.
International exchanges
We hope that every student participates in an international visit of some kind during their school career. In addition to MFL exchanges in France, Spain, Germany, and China, we have expanded our curriculum exchanges to include Argentina, Guatemala and Canada, enabling our pupils to develop a wider understanding of the world.
Wren 300
To celebrate the 300th anniversary of Sir Christopher Wren’s birth, Wren 300 enabled 250 children from ten of the City of London Family of Schools to participate in a varied series of workshops. These workshops resulted in learning in various facets, from music and art – which was displayed at Guildhall – to maths and creative writing. The Wren 300 project has provided extraordinary opportunities for pupils to celebrate, understand and collaborate in spaces at the heart of our cultural identity and heritage.
FOS Coaching Day
Each spring term we host colleagues in middle leadership positions from the Family of Schools to take part in a bespoke day of Coaching training. Our programme helps to equip school middle leaders with essential skills to lead effectively in complex educational environments.
Kerridge Lectures
The launch of the Kerridge Lecture series has advanced the opportunity to examine cutting-edge biological and medical research. The series is named after alumna Phyllis Margaret Tookey Kerridge, whose work to invent new medical technologies has improved the quality of life for millions worldwide. We have welcomed several high-profile lecturers who have shared their time and expertise with students and staff.
Dragons' Den sustainability event
At the beginning of summer term, we host our annual Dragon’s Den Sustainability event, bringing together year 5 pupils from our partner primary schools. The event is always supported by CLSG year 7 pupils. They each lead a mixed-school team and work together to design and present an innovative eco-friendly product which will tackle key problems surrounding climate change and pollution. After presenting each group receives tailored feedback from our guest judge Christopher Pritchard, Vice President, Strategic Initiatives – Climate Risk and Opportunity at Macquarie Asset Management.
Partnership with Bow School
We welcomed year 7 pupils from Bow School to City, as part of an ongoing partnership between our schools and CLS over the past four years. These students collaborated throughout a pupil-led journalism session, as well as advancing their critical thinking in a biology ‘skulls’ session.
The Forget Me Not Cafe
In 2024, we launched our partnership with The Forget Me Not Cafe, which provides services for people with long-term memory issues. At multiple points in the academic year pupils from City will visit the cafe to give performances. This year performances included scenes from The Crucible, as well as dances from spring term’s Gym and Dance Display.
International Women's Day: We Are Cityzens event & panel
To celebrate International Women’s Day in spring 2026, our politics department hosted a ‘We Are Cityzens’ event, inviting pupils from City of London Academy Highgate Hill to join CLSG pupils for an afternoon designing their own political campaigns. Afterwards, pupils got to hear from a panel of speakers with different roles in politics, who shared insights about how they got into politics as well as the highlights and challenges of their respective careers.
Green Shoots Tree Songs project
Our new nature songs programme brought together over 120 pupils from three Tower Hamlets state primary schools (Osmani, William Davis and English Martyrs). Joining musical forces with our junior choir, they sang both old and contemporary songs inspired by trees, accompanied by sounds generated by trees themselves through an app.
Leadership Day
In the second half of summer term, we welcome year 12 pupil leaders from across our Family of Schools to City’s annual Leadership Day. Working in mixed-school groups, students work with external leadership coaches, and explore the strengths and impact of different leadership styles. The day culminates in an exciting treasure hunt competition across the City, where students put their newfound leadership insights into practice.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prize Day - City of London School for Girls
pageCache.text:
Prize Day
Our annual Prize Day at the Guildhall brought together students, staff, families and friends to celebrate the incredible achievements of our pupils across academic and co-curricular life. From inspiring musical and dance performances to a brilliant excerpt from The 39 Steps - Even More Abridged by our talented year 8 students, the ceremony showcased the creativity, dedication and spirit of our community. Following moving speeches from the Lord Mayor Locum Tenens, our headmistress Jenny Brown and our Head Girl Arianne the celebrations continued with a delicious tea in the Old Library. Congratulations to all of this year's prize winners. We are immensely proud of everything you have achieved.

What happens when students are given the freedom to explore a topic that genuinely fascinates them? For our year 13 EPQ students, the answer is a year of fulfilling independent research, intellectual challenge and fascinating discoveries. Last week students presented their final projects, exploring topics ranging from ancient burial rituals and robotic surgery to reparations for the Marshall Islands and the experiences of female domestic workers in Hong Kong. Meet four of our students and discover where their curiosity took them.
